The method is reasonably well motivated relative to raster-order AR, MaskGIT-style bidirectional masked modeling, and RandAR-style randomized AR, and the paper includes useful architectural ablations, sampling-step studies, and implementation hyperparameters.

The novelty over XLNet-style two-stream attention and RandAR is meaningful but somewhat incremental; the paper should more directly isolate the contribution from prior randomized AR methods under matched training, tokenizer, parameter count, and compute.

The inference procedure changes the training-time causal factorization by using block-wise parallel prediction and local bidirectional context. strengths: The paper tackles an important bottleneck in visual autoregressive generation: rigid raster-order decoding and poor parallelism. The proposed decoupling of content representations from target-position queries is a clear and plausible architectural idea.

The ImageNet class-conditional results are strong on paper: ARPG reports competitive or better FID than recent visual AR baselines while substantially improving throughput and memory at comparable model scales.

The submission includes several useful ablations, including decoding steps, attention pattern, decoder allocation, shared KV projection, and positional encoding. The appendix gives architecture/hyperparameter details and pseudo-code.

The method is demonstrated across several settings beyond class-conditional generation, including 512px generation, text-to-image, controllable generation, inpainting, outpainting, and resolution expansion.
weaknesses: The main claims are broader than the evidence. Zero-shot inpainting/outpainting/resolution expansion are supported almost entirely by qualitative examples, with no quantitative metrics or strong baselines, despite being framed as a key advantage.

The efficiency comparison is under-specified and potentially incomplete: it considers only token generation, uses a single batch size/hardware setting, omits end-to-end latency including tokenizer/decoder and conditioning costs, and does not clearly state whether all baselines were reprofiled identically.

The theoretical justification is weak. The proof mainly shows that unmasked-token queries receive no direct loss in masked modeling, but this does not establish that masked modeling is inherently inefficient or that attention to mask tokens is generally redundant. The claim that block-wise inference does not compromise the causal probabilistic model is also not rigorously justified.

Fairness of comparisons is not fully convincing. Baselines differ in parameter count, tokenization, training data, training budget, resolution handling, and sampling/search details. The text-to-image comparison is especially weak: ARPG is only comparable to LlamaGen and below SD-v1.5 on the reported overall GenEval metric, despite strong efficiency claims.

The controllable-generation evaluation relies mainly on FID and excludes adapter parameters, which weakens claims about controllability quality and model efficiency. Structural adherence metrics for Canny/depth conditioning are missing.

Novelty is somewhat incremental relative to RandAR, XLNet-style permutation modeling, masked-token generation, and decoder-decoder/cross-attention designs. The paper positions against these works, but the conceptual distinction is not always as strong as the claimed contribution suggests.

Reproducibility is limited for a top-tier submission: there is no clear code/model release statement, the 4M text-to-image subset is not precisely specified, and several implementation details needed to reproduce throughput and FID are missing.

strengths: Clear and relevant contribution: the two-pass design separating content KV construction from position-guided queries is a plausible way to support randomized parallel decoding while retaining causal-style caching benefits.
weaknesses: Several important claims are overstated or insufficiently supported. Zero-shot inpainting, outpainting, editing, and resolution expansion are shown only qualitatively, with no quantitative metrics or task-specific baselines, despite being central advertised benefits.
